title: Rachida Dati Backs Michel Barnier: Why She Renounced Her Candidacy
text:
PARIS, france – Rachida Dati may soon step aside from the partial legislative elections in Paris’s 2nd district, paving the way for Michel Barnier to run unopposed on September 21 and 28. This potential withdrawal comes wiht a notable guarantee: dati would be the official Republican (LR) candidate for the Paris mayoral race in 2026.
Dati Seeks 2026 Mayoral Nod
Rachida Dati is reportedly seeking assurances from her party for a 2026 mayoral bid in Paris.
This internal political maneuver,confirmed by a Republican leader to Agence France-Presse,would end the brewing “fratricidal duel” between Dati and Barnier. The party is preparing to officially back Dati for the city hall in 2026.
Did you know?-The 2nd district of Paris has historically been a stronghold for right-wing candidates, making Barnier’s unopposed run a significant advantage for the LR party.
“Rachida Dati wanted to be reassured so that she was the candidate of LR at the municipal elections in Paris,” explained the party manager. This agreement would allow Barnier to run alone in the 2nd district, a traditional right-wing stronghold that faced a challenge from a Socialist Party candidate last year.
The Republican National Inauguration Commission is scheduled to meet Thursday evening to formalize this arrangement. Their decision follows the validation of Barnier’s candidacy a month prior, despite Dati, the mayor of the 7th arrondissement, also announcing her intention to compete.
Dati had reiterated her commitment to running in a recent interview, but the deal appears to shift the landscape. She had previously criticized Barnier’s candidacy as “instrumentalized” in the 2nd district,where the election of the Macronist deputy Jean Laussucq was invalidated by the Constitutional Council due to campaign finance irregularities.
Pro tip:-political parties often negotiate candidate placements to avoid internal competition and maximize their chances of winning key elections, as seen in this agreement between Dati and Barnier.
Dati, who joined Gabriel Attal’s government as Minister of Culture in january 2024, rejoined the LR party after a period of exclusion in 2024. however, her political ambitions are now shadowed by a recent legal setback. On July 22, Dati was convicted in a corruption and influence-peddling trial. The court found her guilty of receiving 900,000 euros between 2010 and 2012 from a Renault-Nissan Alliance subsidiary for consulting work that appeared to be largely unfulfilled during her time as a lawyer and Member of the European Parliament.
Dati has appealed the ruling,and a preliminary hearing to set a trial date is scheduled for September 29. The outcome of this legal challenge could significantly impact her future political career, including her prospects for the 2026 Paris mayoral race.
reader question:-How might this legal challenge affect Dati’s standing within the LR party and her ability to effectively campaign for the Paris mayoral election?
